title: Dr. S. Radhakrishnan and Joseph Stalin: The Philosopher-Diplomat in Moscow — 1952
summary: In April 1952, India's ambassador to Moscow, philosopher Dr. S. Radhakrishnan, held an extraordinary farewell meeting with Soviet dictator Joseph Stalin, offering profound moral counsel.
keywords: Historical Dialogue 142: காந்தியும் “Scandal Times” இதழும்: “மிக மதிப்புள்ளதை எடுத்துவிட்டேன்”
full_text:
On April 5, 1952, at the height of the Cold War, a historic diplomatic farewell took place inside the Kremlin in Moscow.

Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, the renowned philosopher serving as India's ambassador to the Soviet Union, was granted a rare private audience with Premier Joseph Stalin. Western diplomats often trembled in the dictator's presence, but Radhakrishnan—clad in his immaculate traditional dhoti and turban—conversed with the calm composure of an Upanishadic teacher.

As their conversation drew to a close, Radhakrishnan looked directly at Stalin and offered an unexpected historical reflection:
"Generalissimo Stalin, in our ancient Indian history, Emperor Ashoka waged a devastating war at Kalinga. He conquered vast lands, but when he gazed upon the battlefield, he realized that military violence can never win the hearts of humanity. He renounced the sword and embraced the path of peace, moral law, and compassion. You, too, have built a colossal empire through struggle. May you, like Ashoka, choose the path of enduring peace for mankind."

Stalin fell silent, deeply moved by the philosopher’s quiet courage. Grasping Radhakrishnan’s hand, the Soviet leader replied softly:
"Professor, you do not speak to me like a maneuvering politician; you speak like a true philosopher and friend of humanity. Your words will stay with me."

As Radhakrishnan departed, Stalin patted him affectionately on the cheek—a gesture unprecedented in Soviet diplomatic history, proving that moral truth transcends geopolitical power.
